ledger.claim: The three telemetry artifacts describe one and the same trip. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown each carry trip TRP-00113; the trace's first fix at 18:47:10 matches the trip_record's started_at of 18:47:10; and the fare's charged_at of 19:23:31 follows the recorded ended_at of 19:23:10. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) — that the artifacts describe the same trip, with matching trip identifier and pickup timestamp — is discharged on the face of the record, so the question is the measurement, not the identity of the trip.

The filed claim measured this trip against the 15.8 km solo-rider figure. POL-RD-12 fixes the baseline for a RYDE_POOL trip at the matched-itinerary optimal recorded on the trip_record — the 19.4 km the platform computed for the pooled route at match time, and which the system message MSG-00113-001 quoted to the rider in-app at 18:42:04, before the vehicle moved, and which the rider read at 18:42:31. The rider does not press the solo figure, which POL-RD-12 says fails on that ground alone, and puts the matched-itinerary figure of 19.4 km in issue instead, as the clause requires.

The distance to be measured is the trace's, not the bill's. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing field and bars citation of trip_record.actual_distance_km for the threshold test, and the trace measures 20.18 km. Measured against the matched-itinerary optimal of 19.4 km, the platform's own derivation puts the excess at 0.78 km, or 4.02%. That is the figure the rider relies on, and the rider cites the trace rather than the 20.2 km rounded copy carried on the trip_record and the fare_breakdown.

Honest concession, because the record does not support the point: an excess of 0.78 km is 0.02 km below the 0.8 km absolute limb of POL-RD-01 and 4.02% is far below its 20% limb, and POL-RD-01 requires both tests to pass. On this trip's own unimpaired trace no route deviation is established, and the rider does not overstate the measurement, ask the tribunal to round it up, or characterise a 20-metre margin as a 28% detour.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 217 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met, so the excess is measured across continuous telemetry rather than inferred across a gap, and no independent-corroboration question under POL-RD-07(ii) arises. Whatever the outcome, it rests on complete GPS data rather than on a data failure.

The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this trip and I disclose the impairment: EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, carries no payload, has issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, so its absence is citable but it can carry no fact. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run on this record, no closure or congestion adjustment raises the matched-itinerary optimal of 19.4 km, and the baseline against which the excess is measured stands where the platform booked it. The rider does not ask for escalation on that absence: POL-RD-13(1) confines POL-RD-10(5) to a missing identifier that a party has actually cited, and no party has cited one.

The profile artifacts are credibility weighting only. POL-GEN-01 provides that no profile field may establish a fact about this trip, and the only profile tests in this category are POL-RD-06's pattern test and POL-RD-08's claim-count test. POL-RD-06 is not engaged at all, because no MATERIAL deviation (over 50% or over 8.0 km) exists on this trace, so the driver's 90-day figures — deviation_flags_90d of 0 across 471 completed trips — decide nothing here in either direction, and this claim rises or falls on the GPS trace alone.

The rider is not a serial claimant whose claim requires corroboration beyond the trace: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the corroboration uplift in POL-RD-08 — which applies only at 4 or more claims in 60 days with 1 or fewer substantiated — is not triggered. No rider-profile counter is used to deny a claim that the trace supports; the rider abandoned the solo-baseline theory of its own motion and asks only that the matched-itinerary excess be measured as POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-12 direct.

This was a RYDE_POOL booking, so the baseline for the POL-RD-01 deviation test is the matched-itinerary optimal of 19.40 km recorded on the trip record — the pooled route the platform computed at match time — and not the solo-rider figure of 15.80 km, which POL-RD-12 carries as reference only. The rider's '28% longer' figure is arithmetic against the wrong field, and POL-RD-12 provides that a claim measuring excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone; the ruling should name both figures so the rider can see why.

Measured against the correct baseline, no deviation is established. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure governing, and the trace records 20.18 km against the 19.40 km matched itinerary: an excess of 0.78 km, or 4.02%. Both establishment tests must pass and neither does — 0.78 km is not greater than 0.8 km, and 4.02% is not greater than 20%. No material deviation arises either, since the excess is far below 50% and 8.0 km. The outcome on the rider's claim is therefore NO_ACTION and the present state of the charge stands.

The one excursion the rider points to — 'the driver went off to Hougang in the middle of my trip' — is the platform-matched co-rider pickup, not a detour. The driver's chat message at 19:03:15 records 'pool booking, picking up the other passenger, app route', and the artifact's admissibility notes record the 90-second standstill at Hougang Central at 19:03:40 where that co-rider boarded. Distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is excluded from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The rider was told of the pooled route in advance: the platform's match notification MSG-00113-001, sent at 18:42:04 and read by the rider at 18:42:31, stated the Hougang pickup and an estimated 19.4 km, some six minutes before the 18:47:10 trip start.

The rider's POL-RD-08 burden fails at its second limb. The identifiers do line up — TRP-00113 is common to the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace's first fix at 18:47:10 matches the recorded start — but limb (b) requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, and the excess measured from this unimpaired trace is 4.02%, below both gates. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver, and no exculpatory clause needs to be invoked for the claim to fail.

The trace on which this measurement rests is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 217 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds. None of limbs (a) to (c) is met, so the corroboration requirement of POL-RD-07(ii) is not engaged and no escalation under POL-RD-10(3) can arise from the trace. The measurement above stands on the trace alone at full weight.

The POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation check, which is the only profile inquiry this category permits, comes back clean and is not even required here because no material deviation is recorded. The driver has 0 deviation flags in the trailing 90 days across 471 completed trips, so no pattern is established: there is no full-refund uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no basis for a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. Both figures are stated so the uplift question is auditable.

There is no billing-integrity defect for POL-RD-09(4) to correct on this fare. The breakdown carries no ERP gantries (erp total 0.00), no airport surcharge, and no line for a gantry or surcharge the trace never touched; the components reconcile to the cent to the 26.83 charged, and the 3.00 pool discount has already been subtracted in the rider's favour. Nothing on the fare awaits a standalone pass-through correction, and the disputed amount of 6.00 is not traceable to any mis-billed line.

No traffic advisory covers this trip window: EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and that impairment is disclosed here. It makes no difference to this side of the case, because the driver never asserts an external traffic cause — his account is the platform-matched pooled itinerary, which is POL-RD-12 and not POL-RD-03. Under POL-RD-13 an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, so the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it and is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger. The case is decidable on the record and should not be escalated.

Neither of the remaining exculpatory clauses changes the arithmetic, so nothing subtracts from or adds to the matched-itinerary baseline. POL-RD-04 is unavailable: the chat log contains no rider instruction to detour — the rider's only message, at 19:02:40, asks 'why are we at hougang' well after the route was set and names no waypoint. POL-RD-05 is unavailable: the trip record shows both amendment timestamps null, amended_optimal_distance_km null, and an unamended pickup and dropoff. The baseline therefore remains the booked matched-itinerary optimal of 19.40 km and the threshold analysis above is final.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: your claim is measured against the wrong baseline, and even on the correct one the deviation does not reach the policy threshold. This was a RYDE_POOL booking (EV-TRIP-00113, vehicle_type RYDE_POOL). Under POL-RD-12 the baseline for a pooled trip is the matched-itinerary optimal the platform quoted at match time — 19.40 km on the trip record — and not the 15.80 km solo-rider figure, which the record carries as reference only. Your '28% longer' figure is arithmetic against the 15.80 km field, and POL-RD-12 says a claim measured that way fails on that ground alone. The governing distance is the GPS trace figure of 20.18 km (EV-GPS-00113, trace_distance_km; POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern and bars citation of the rounded 20.2 km copy). Excess = 20.18 − 19.40 = 0.78 km, or 4.02%. POL-RD-01 requires both more than 0.8 km absolute and more than 20%; 0.78 km falls 20 metres short of the absolute limb and 4.02% is far below the percentage limb. No deviation is established, so no refund arises under POL-RD-02. The Hougang stop you pointed to is not a detour: it is the platform-matched co-rider pickup, recorded as a 90-second standstill at Hougang Central at 19:03:40, and POL-RD-12 excludes distance spent collecting a co-rider on a matched pooled itinerary before the threshold test is applied. The platform told you of the pooled route and its 19.40 km estimate at 18:42:04, six minutes before the 18:47:10 start. To the driver: your account is accepted. The matched-itinerary baseline of 19.40 km stands, the Hougang leg is platform-matched and not chargeable to you, and no exculpatory clause needed to be invoked because the claim fails on measurement. POL-RD-04 is unavailable (the only rider message, at 19:02:40, asks a question and names no waypoint) and POL-RD-05 is unavailable (amendment timestamps and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null), so nothing adjusts the baseline. On billing integrity, EV-FARE-00113 shows no ERP gantry, no airport surcharge and no unmatched line; its components reconcile to the 26.83 charged and the 3.00 pool discount is already applied, so POL-RD-09(4) has nothing to correct. EV-ADVIS-00113-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT; that absence is not an escalation trigger, because no party asserted an external traffic cause — your account is the pool match under POL-RD-12 — so POL-RD-03 was never invoked and POL-RD-13(1) confirms the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it, leaving POL-RD-10(5) unengaged. EV-GPS-00113 is unimpaired for policy purposes (217 fixes, 100% coverage, 10-second interval, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s), so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged. No material deviation exists, so POL-RD-06 is not required; in any event the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 471 completed trips, so no repeat pattern and no POL-RD-06(c) referral. No profile field was used to establish any fact about this trip (POL-GEN-01). Outcome: NO_ACTION — the charge of 26.83 stands as it is, nothing is refunded, no compensation is due, and the monetary effect is zero, below the 8.00 execution threshold. The earlier decisions P-0001 and P-0002 are PARTIAL_REFUND on a shared clause set, but each rested on a POL-RD-01 excess that was actually established; here this trip's trace yields 0.78 km, below the absolute limb, so there is no deviation to refund.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
